title: Choose Fisher's visual world
question: Which world makes quantitative systems engineering feel unmistakably Fisher—not a generic consultancy?

options.label: Exchange Operations Ledger
options.lineage: exchange bulletins, order-flow ledgers, and production runbooks
options.thesis: Fisher's work becomes an inspectable operating record from research through monitoring.
options.viewport: A dated masthead and four-stage system trace lead directly into Alchemist and the trading-data pipeline.
options.risk: The ledger can become costume if rules and labels outrank Fisher's actual evidence.

raised.raise: Use one unmistakable signal color per system state, never decorative color.
Give every project a strict evidence label with role, stack, and destination.
Make the research-to-production sequence irreversible and easy to follow.
Let motion explain system flow while reduced motion preserves the full reading.
Own the first viewport with one decisive composition instead of nested cards.
Stage the consulting action as a clear final threshold, not a persistent sales pitch.

options.label: Systems Review Wall
options.lineage: architecture reviews, reliability diagrams, and control-room trace boards
options.thesis: The homepage behaves like an engineering review where every claim connects to proof.
options.viewport: Fisher's introduction anchors a live architecture trace linking research, data, execution, and monitoring to real projects.
options.risk: Architecture diagrams are familiar in engineering portfolios and need Fisher's writing and evidence to avoid sameness.

options.label: Signal Partition
options.thesis: Each stage is a pane: clear at rest, saturated only when its evidence is active.
options.viewport: A full-height four-bay system wall gives each stage one statement and one linked project.
options.case: It matches the system map's clarity, but its craft identity is less immediate to trading-firm visitors.
options.risk: Without disciplined labels, the panes can read as an art studio instead of quantitative infrastructure.

options.label: Darkroom Sequence
options.thesis: Research emerges through deliberate stages before it can become production evidence.
options.viewport: Compose, expose, develop, fix, and monitor form one linear scroll sequence.
options.case: The process metaphor weakens recognition of trading infrastructure and makes the system map less literal.
options.kept: A staged progression in which each step earns the next.
options.risk: The amber atmosphere can overwhelm accessible reading and technical specificity.

options.label: Archive Stack
options.lineage: sneaker archive walls and indexed box labels
options.thesis: Projects become labeled evidence packages that visitors can pull open.
options.viewport: A wall of project labels opens into details, links, and technical scope.
options.case: The archive interaction is clear, but its fashion-retail signal misses both quantitative engineering and consulting intent.
options.kept: Every project needs a consistent evidence label, not a vague showcase card.
options.risk: The box metaphor turns serious infrastructure work into collectible merchandise.

options.label: Shader Portal
options.thesis: A living field makes the path through Fisher's work feel spatial and continuous.
options.viewport: A full-screen shader sits behind a sparse introduction and corner navigation.
options.case: It loses both axes: the form signals creative agency and hides the concrete system proof trading visitors need.
options.kept: Motion should expose flow and state, not decorate the page.
options.risk: This is the clearest path back to the generic-agency failure boundary.

options.label: Floating Field
options.lineage: saturated startup fields with detached capsule controls
options.thesis: One bold color owns the viewport while projects sit on floating content slabs.
options.viewport: A bright field carries Fisher's oversized introduction above a rising project panel.
options.case: The first impression is clear, but it reads as a generic SaaS launch rather than a trusted production engineer.
options.kept: One decisive first-viewport composition with no timid card grid.
options.risk: Pills, blobs, and overshoot motion would erase the precision the brand needs.

options.label: Premiere Threshold
options.lineage: Art Deco cinema lobbies at premiere hour
options.thesis: Each section becomes a staged threshold leading toward the consulting conversation.
options.viewport: A symmetrical marquee introduces Fisher before stepped thresholds reveal his work.
options.case: The ceremony is memorable, but entertainment and luxury signals obscure engineering trust and product clarity.
options.kept: The contact action should feel like an earned final threshold.
options.risk: Ornament would become the story while Fisher's evidence becomes supporting copy.

canonCard.label: Dark Fintech Terminal
canonCard.thesis: Ship the category standard: dark dashboard surfaces, compact metrics, and electric status color.
canonCard.viewport: A dark hero presents Fisher beside a compact research-to-execution dashboard and project metrics.
canonCard.risk: Immediately legible to trading firms, but interchangeable with fintech products and developer templates.
